symptom: The v352 static negative-catalog contract test pinned all 18 case IDs, mutations, fixture states and first denial codes, but accepted changes or removal of authoritySeparation and usageRules. A modified catalog could say caller-selected keys, caller FINAL or protocol approval suffice, or delete the no-production rule, while all existing catalog tests still passed. This is a specification-integrity gap only; no independent verifier or production/scoring path was executed.
lesson: Freezing individual negative cases is insufficient when a catalog also carries global authority-custody and usage restrictions. Those global policy statements can be weakened independently of case identities, expected denials and authorization flags.
guardrail: Pin the exact independent-witness, settlement, caller-claim and protocol custody statements and all usage restrictions in a separately maintained static test expectation. Add deliberate mutation, deletion and addition tests for those fields. Changes to the contract require an explicit reviewed update; a static catalog PASS is never independent attestation, scoring or production authority.
